note: Rewritten from Light 1932, pp. 379—380; original in English; the soldier reached the author, collected by Gable, only just before the paper went to press, so the species was originally based on the alate alone; the soldier measurement table is shared with A. minimus, and only the two columns for this species are given here. The original "gula" is rendered postmentum.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alate generally brown above and yellow below, head, pronotum and body covered with a thick, dense coat of long white hairs; the smallest known alate of the genus. Soldier small, head capsule slightly more than 1 mm long and about 0.85 mm wide, head index about 0.8; head rectangular, sides parallel or slightly convex, constriction index 1.0 or slightly less; head high, with the sides and the rear steep and nearly vertical, giving the head a box-like shape. It differs from A. minimus mainly in the short, broad mandibles, the box-like soldier head and the smaller alate. In 1932 the author noted that Banks had wrongly placed the alate of this species under his A. arizonensis.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Generally brown above and yellow below; antennae and postclypeus smoky yellow; labrum, tarsi and apices of the tibiae yellow; abdominal sternites pale brown; head, pronotum and body covered with a thick, dense coat of long white hairs. Head short, rounded behind the eyes. Fontanelle very small, narrowly oval, slightly pointed behind; broadly fused in front with a short, wide frontal line. Muscle impressions faint; the oblique impressions are visible only from about halfway between the end of the frontal line of the fontanelle and the anterior margin of the head capsule. Postclypeus as in the original fig. Z. Eyes elongate anteroposteriorly; about half their short diameter from the lower margin of the head and about half their long diameter or a little more from the upper margin, and about twice their long diameter from the posterior margin. Ocelli large, length about 2/3 that of the eye; width more than half the length; close to the eyes and less than their short diameter apart. Pronotum short; in dorsal view length about equal to half the width; sides deflexed; anterior corners broadly rounded; sides convex, strongly receding into a narrow, straight posterior margin. Wings pale brown, the line behind the radial sector and the basal branches of the cubitus dark brown. Measurements (mm): head length including the labrum 1.02; head capsule length 0.69; head width across the eyes 0.84; eye length 0.23; ocellus length 0.12; ocellus width 0.07; postclypeus length 0.21; postclypeus width 0.38; postclypeus index 0.55; pronotum length 0.39; pronotum width 0.75.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Small; head capsule slightly more than 1 mm long and about 0.85 mm wide, head index about 0.8; head rectangular, sides parallel or slightly convex, constriction index 1.0 or slightly less; head high, with the sides and the rear steep and nearly vertical, giving the head a box-like shape; posterior corners very short and rounded; posterior margin slightly convex. Mandibles stout and short, head-mandible index less than 0.6; mandibles strongly curved at the outer third. Tooth similar to that of A. minimus but, because the mandibles are shortened, situated a little below the middle of the mandible. Sides of the postmentum nearly straight, postmentum constriction index about 0.95. Measurements (mm; the two soldiers A and B of this species, placed beside A. minimus in the original table): head length 1.08, 1.05; maximum head width 0.87, 0.84; minimum head width 0.87, 0.78; mandible length 0.61, 0.60; postmentum length 0.55, 0.55; maximum postmentum width 0.275, 0.27; minimum postmentum width 0.26, 0.255; head index 0.80, 0.80; head constriction index 1.00, 0.93; head-mandible index 0.56, 0.58; postmentum constriction index 0.94, 0.94; minimum mandible curvature 0.0725, 0.0725; mandible curvature index 0.12, 0.12.
